facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man
history of coronary artery disease status post–bypass surgery
emphysema
chest pain, dyspnea, cough, night sweats, and a 20-pound unintentional weight loss
Physical examination was unremarkable
Laboratory studies, including a complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic profile, were within normal limits
a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass measuring 1.2 × 8.6 × 10.7 cm
causing mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins
Transbronchial needle aspiration of a right hilar mass showed benign bronchial cells
EUS-guided FNA of an oval, hypoechoic posterior mediastinal lesion (68 × 70 mm) obtained a core biopsy that demonstrated a spindle cell neoplasm with large nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3
Somatic genetic analysis of cKIT and PDGFRA revealed no mutations, and germline testing was positive for NF1, suggesting wild-type GIST

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass and a spindle cell neoplasm with positive immunohistochemical staining, are consistent with a diagnosis of GIST.
The patient's germline testing was positive for NF1, suggesting a diagnosis of NF1, which is a genetic disorder that can increase the risk of developing GIST.
The patient's history of emphysema and symptoms of chest pain, dyspnea, and cough are consistent with a diagnosis of COPD.
The patient's history of coronary artery disease status post-bypass surgery is consistent with a diagnosis of coronary artery disease.
The patient's imaging findings, including multiple pulmonary nodules and a pleural-based lesion, are consistent with a diagnosis of pulmonary metastasis.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass and pulmonary nodules, are consistent with a diagnosis of sarcoidosis.
The patient's imaging findings, including a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass and hilar lymph nodes, are consistent with a diagnosis of lymphoma.
The patient's symptoms, including chest pain and dyspnea, are consistent with a diagnosis of pulmonary embolism.
